problem: For nonzero real numbers a, b, c, and d satisfying 6/a=6/b+6/c-6/d, which expression is equivalent to d?

bad.why: Substituting four rational expressions into the equation by hand is heavy fraction algebra; Desmos evaluates them at once.
'Which expression is equivalent to d' is a rearrangement, not a word situation to translate.

algebraFirst.description: Divides by 6, isolates 1/d=1/b+1/c-1/a, combines over abc to (ab+ac-bc)/(abc), and takes the reciprocal, often without explaining the flip.

explanationNotes: Explain that the equation must hold for every allowed a, b, c, so picking simple nonzero values (a=2, b=3, c=5) turns each choice into a number; the right choice is the one that makes the original equation balance, showing 0. Pick values that keep every denominator nonzero and give four different results.
notes: Paraphrase of Bedrock Prep hard Problem 20, Rearranging Terms; choices are original distractor variants. Divide by 6, rearrange to 1/d=1/b+1/c-1/a, combine terms over abc to get (ab+ac-bc)/(abc), then reciprocate. Every denominator must be nonzero. Explain each fraction move; Desmos is only useful if it actually simplifies identifying the equivalent expression. Category index: https://www.bedrockprep.com/problems
